- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips sharply, delay or dampen forecast adjustment for 1–2 periods.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the following 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–15% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “positive → negative” transitions, model tends to lag in correcting downward; anticipate and preemptively lower forecast 1–2 periods ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), apply a “sentiment-weighted bias correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% for each negative sentiment day in the last 7 days.
